description: Decision-path and step-reduction wins that jev structurally cannot do because its model is remote (levers 2, 3, 4). (2) Widen src/laya/goal.ts so MORE TYPE_TEXT values resolve locally with ZERO network (deleting jev's most expensive per-step operation, its remote text LLM): dates, cities, emails, and quoted multi-word strings. (3) Generalize policy.ts batching/composition so a multi-field goal + unambiguous next control collapses into fewer decisions. (4) Speculative local DECIDE during browser settle: overlap engine.decide with the settle window (free for a local model; jev cannot safely fire a speculative NETWORK call per step) and use the result only if the page is unchanged when settle completes (discard on drift, guarded by the FEAT-002 freshness check). All additive and behind the existing flags where they change the hot path; the offline stub suite stays green.
steps: In src/laya/goal.ts: widen the goal grammar so more values resolve locally without a model/LLM call, keeping every helper pure and side-effect-free and preserving existing behavior. (a) In goalAssignments, additionally recognize common field synonyms and unquoted multi-word values that stop at a clause boundary rather than the first space where safe (e.g. `city is New York`, `name is Ada Lovelace`), and recognize date-shaped and email-shaped values without requiring quotes (an email like a@b.com and an ISO/`MM/DD/YYYY` date should map even unquoted, resolving the documented 'quote values with dots' limitation for these specific shapes). (b) Keep the search-intent fallback conservative as-is. Add focused unit tests in a goal test (extend the existing goal/policy test coverage) for: unquoted email, unquoted date, quoted multi-word city, and a two-field name+email goal - each asserting fieldValueFromGoal / goalAssignments extract the right values. Do NOT loosen matching so far that it dumps values into arbitrary fields (keep the multi-field no-name-match safety).

In src/autopilot/policy.ts: generalize the deterministic composition. (a) The FILL_FORM batch already fires for >=2 unfilled goal fields; extend it so that when, after batching, exactly one unambiguous submit/search control exists AND the goal has a success/search intent, the SAME step sequence is expressed with the fewest decisions the current Decision union allows (batch fill, then submit) - keep each emitted Decision individually valid (no illegal composite states). (b) Add/extend policy unit tests (following test/autopilot*.test.ts patterns) proving a 3+ field goal batches into one FILL_FORM and that single-field goals keep the TYPE_TEXT path unchanged. Do not change RULE_CONFIDENCE or the rule ordering semantics.

In src/autopilot/loop.ts: add speculative-decide-during-settle. Today the loop overlaps a speculative CAPTURE with the settle probe (T4.1 prefetchedSnapshot). Extend that: when settleProbe runs AND the speculative capture reports no change (page settled, snapshot current) AND a decision engine is available, ALSO run policySeed/engine.decide against the prefetched state concurrently with the probe, and cache the resulting speculative Decision. At the TOP of the next iteration, if the prefetched snapshot is reused (page unchanged) AND the FEAT-002 freshness check confirms the speculative decision's target is still fresh, USE the cached decision instead of recomputing (skip the redundant decide). On ANY drift (probe changed, target guard stale, or auto-dismiss ran) DISCARD the speculative decision and decide fresh. This must be purely an optimization: the observed decision sequence and outcomes are identical to not speculating; only the wall-clock overlap changes. Gate it so it only activates when fastLoop is on (keeps the default path untouched) OR add a narrow guard so existing autopilot tests are byte-identical. Add a test asserting a settled-page run reuses the speculative decision (no double decide) and that a drifted page discards it.

Run pnpm run typecheck, pnpm run build, pnpm test. Confirm the offline stub suite stays green (same default counts) and the new goal/policy/speculation tests pass. If a real model bundle is available via LAYA_MODEL_DIR, optionally run the gated real-weights test to confirm the widened grammar still resolves values locally; if not available, note that the widening is model-independent (it is pure goal parsing, not a model change) so the stub suite is sufficient evidence.
acceptance_criteria: fieldValueFromGoal/goalAssignments resolve unquoted emails, unquoted dates, quoted multi-word values, and multi-field name+email goals (asserted in unit tests) without regressing existing cases.
A 3+ field goal produces a single FILL_FORM batch; single-field goals keep TYPE_TEXT (asserted).
Speculative decide during settle is reused when the page is unchanged and the target is fresh, and discarded on drift, with identical observed decision sequence vs not speculating (asserted).
The offline stub suite pass/skip counts match the prior baseline (no regressions); new tests pass.
No em dashes in new content; goal.ts stays pure.
verification: Run `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run build`; both exit 0.
Run `pnpm test`; the default suite matches the running baseline and the new goal/policy/speculation tests pass.
Run the specific new test files via `pnpm vitest run` and confirm the widened-grammar, batching, and speculation assertions pass.
